problems.stem: Which resume bullet gives a reader the strongest, most verifiable evidence of impact?
options: Responsible for spreadsheets
Built a 3-tab Excel budget tracker with VLOOKUP that cut the club's monthly reconciliation time from 2 hours to 20 minutes
Hard worker who is good with computers
Did various data tasks as needed
problems.explanation: A strong bullet names the artifact, the skill, and a measurable result a reader can picture and verify. Vague duty statements carry no evidence.

problems.stem: You took one short tutorial in Python. Which resume phrasing is both truthful and useful?
options: Expert Python developer
Completed an introductory Python course; wrote a 40-line script that cleaned a 500-row CSV
Mastered all of Python
Python since birth
problems.explanation: Truthful framing states the actual scope (intro course, a concrete script) so a reader is not misled. Overclaiming expertise fails the first technical question.

problems.stem: An AI tool rewrites your resume and invents a bullet: 'Led a team of 12 to launch a national campaign.' You never did this. What is the right action?
options: Keep it; it sounds impressive and AI wrote it
Delete the fabricated bullet and keep only claims you can back with real evidence; note that AI was used for wording only
Keep it but lower the number to 6
Submit it and explain later if asked
problems.explanation: AI will happily fabricate accomplishments. You stay accountable for truthfulness: remove invented claims and disclose that AI helped with wording, not facts.

problems.stem: You are tailoring one resume for a data-analyst posting that lists Excel and visualization. Which revision shows role fit?
options: Lead with an unrelated babysitting bullet because it came first chronologically
Move the Excel dashboard and chart-design bullets to the top and trim bullets unrelated to data work
Add every job you ever had in full detail to look experienced
Use a rainbow color scheme to stand out
problems.explanation: Role fit means surfacing the evidence the specific posting asks for. Promoting the relevant bullets and trimming the rest signals fit better than length or decoration.

problems.stem: Your GitHub Pages portfolio lists a project as 'Built a website.' Which revision gives a reviewer verifiable evidence?
options: Add a stylish screenshot of the homepage next to the claim.
Link the live URL and state what it shows: 'My CAT 100 data story (live at the linked page) with the published chart and source note.'
Change the wording to 'Built a professional, responsive website.'
Move the claim higher on the page so it is seen first.
problems.explanation: On a published portfolio, the strongest evidence is the live artifact itself: a working link a reviewer can open plus a sentence naming what it demonstrates. A screenshot is unverifiable and ages; adjectives inflate without proving; placement changes salience, not evidence.
